intro: Armenian media focus on Prime Minister Pashinyan's political future and peace negotiations with Azerbaijan, while international outlets highlight a historic trilateral summit between the leaders of China, Russia, and the United States. Domestic coverage also addresses economic forecasts, missing persons from the 44-day war, and cultural events.

topics.title: Pashinyan links political future to constitutional changes and peace deal
topics.text: Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan stated he will step down if constitutional changes fail and will not seek reelection after an Armenia-Azerbaijan peace agreement. The opposition characterized his resignation offer as a trap, while a former government insider criticized his peace and EU policies. Pashinyan also presented an ultimatum regarding the opposition and categorically denied accusations of handing over Syunik territories.

topics.title: Historic trilateral summit held between Xi, Putin, and Trump
topics.text: The leaders of China, Russia, and the United States held a trilateral meeting in China, issuing a joint declaration on peace. Chinese President Xi Jinping urged world powers to respect sovereignty and called for a complete ban on nuclear weapons. The summit was described as historic by international observers and Armenian state media.

topics.title: Armenia addresses fate of missing persons from 44-day war
topics.text: Authorities confirmed approximately 1,000 persons remain missing from the 2020 conflict, with 4,005 bone samples examined for identification. The International Commission on Missing Persons pledged support, while Azerbaijan's presidential aide stated they are still waiting for Armenia to disclose locations of mass graves. Pashinyan emphasized that finding answers for families remains a priority.

topics.title: Armenia invited to 2026 G20 Summit in Miami
topics.text: Armenia has received an invitation to attend the 2026 G20 Summit in Miami, with Prime Minister Pashinyan expected to participate. Reports indicate Azerbaijan has also been invited to the summit. The invitation marks a significant diplomatic engagement for Armenia on the global economic stage.

topics.title: Central Bank warns of inflation impact from potential gas price hike
topics.text: The Central Bank of Armenia governor stated a hypothetical 10% increase in Russian natural gas prices could lead to 0.6% inflation. The governor also stressed the importance of budget reserves in addressing potential macroeconomic risks. The government simultaneously approved its action plan for 2026-2031.

topics.title: Security Council Secretary to visit Azerbaijan next month
topics.text: Armenian Security Council Secretary Armen Grigoryan announced a planned visit to Azerbaijan next month. The visit comes amid ongoing peace negotiations and follows Pashinyan's statements regarding constitutional changes and territorial integrity. The government also approved a new system to monitor real estate agents and property deals.

topics.title: "Ancient Armenia" exhibition to open at Athens Acropolis Museum
topics.text: An exhibition titled "Ancient Armenia" is set to open at the Acropolis Museum in Athens, showcasing Armenian historical artifacts. The event represents a significant cultural diplomacy initiative. Separately, Armenia is preparing to host performances by at least two world-renowned artists in 2027.
